$schema_note: Benchmark and random-null definitions. The B0-B6 / A1-A6 IDs are TRD v1.1 FINAL section 49's own canonical benchmark/ablation matrix, reused verbatim -- not reinvented. Archetype-specific IDs (prefixed BQ/BH/BR/BC/BA) are additions for comparisons the canonical B/A matrix does not name explicitly, needed because the archetype-level hypotheses in hypotheses.json are more granular than the six canonical ablation steps. None of these carry invented performance numbers -- they are comparison *definitions*, to be run once the backtester (Phase 6) exists.

canonical_trd_benchmarks.name: Mechanical CSP
canonical_trd_benchmarks.description: Research-grid DTE/delta + fixed management. Simple premium-selling baseline.

canonical_trd_benchmarks.name: Basic Wheel
canonical_trd_benchmarks.description: CSP -> assignment -> immediate/simple CC. Lifecycle baseline.

canonical_trd_benchmarks.name: Fixed time-exit
canonical_trd_benchmarks.description: Fixed time-exit / 21-DTE style variant where applicable. Time-management benchmark.

canonical_trd_benchmarks.name: Random-entry matched
canonical_trd_benchmarks.description: Random entry matched by ticker/DTE/structure/size. Tests whether timing/selection adds value.

canonical_trd_benchmarks.name: Buy-and-hold assigned underlying
canonical_trd_benchmarks.description: Tests whether Wheel management adds value after assignment.

canonical_trd_benchmarks.name: + ownership model
canonical_trd_benchmarks.description: B1 + ownership model. Incremental ownership value.

canonical_trd_benchmarks.name: + volatility/surface features
canonical_trd_benchmarks.description: A1 + volatility/surface features. Incremental vol value.

canonical_trd_benchmarks.name: + regime model
canonical_trd_benchmarks.description: A2 + regime model. Conditional regime value.

canonical_trd_benchmarks.name: + expert priors
canonical_trd_benchmarks.description: A3 + expert priors. Incremental expert prior value.

archetype_specific_benchmarks.name: Premium/IV-rank-only CSP selection
archetype_specific_benchmarks.description: Select CSP candidates purely by highest premium or IV rank, no ownership_acceptability or p_severe_drawdown screen. Same underlying universe and sizing rules as the variant it is compared against. Counterfactual for H-Q-01 and H-Q-02.

archetype_specific_benchmarks.name: Fixed single-delta conventional CSP
archetype_specific_benchmarks.description: Always selects the single closest-to-0.20 (or closest-to-0.25) delta contract within the DTE window, ignoring the multi-band lattice in theta_q_lattice.py entirely. This is a CONTROL specifically because the research brief prohibits ever choosing only one delta band as the production lattice (theta_q_lattice.LatticeConfig enforces at least two bands at construction time) -- BQ-2 exists to let the multi-band lattice prove it adds value over the single-delta habit, not to license using a single delta.

archetype_specific_benchmarks.name: THETA-Q v0 transparent baseline itself
archetype_specific_benchmarks.description: bots/theta/quant/models/theta_q_baseline.py run as-is, with no learned model behind ownership_acceptability or p_severe_drawdown (i.e. exactly what the module computes today). This is the control the future calibrated entry-outcome model (TRD section 17) must beat before it is trusted as more than academically interesting -- the heuristic answers 'does sophisticated THETA actually beat something simple', it is not itself a candidate for the production decision rule.

archetype_specific_benchmarks.name: Fixed 30-60 DTE conventional CSP
archetype_specific_benchmarks.description: THETA_CONVENTIONAL's own default DTE lattice, run on the same underlying(s) proposed for a Hold-the-Strike cohort. Counterfactual for H-H-01 -- tests whether the 2-5 DTE regime actually beats the conventional regime on the same names, rather than assuming it from IWM Hold the Strike's reputation alone.

archetype_specific_benchmarks.name: Always hold to expiration
archetype_specific_benchmarks.description: No early close or roll under any condition; only expire/assign/exercise resolves the position. Counterfactual for H-R-01 (the active-management thesis).

archetype_specific_benchmarks.name: Always close/roll at fixed 50% profit capture
archetype_specific_benchmarks.description: Mirrors canonical B3 but stated as the explicit opposing baseline for H-R-02 (the patience thesis) -- if patience is right, BR-2 should underperform hold-to-cycle on a capital-day-adjusted basis.

archetype_specific_benchmarks.name: Covered call selected by max annualized yield only
archetype_specific_benchmarks.description: No trade-off against retained upside, call-away regret, or event risk. Counterfactual for H-C-01.

archetype_specific_benchmarks.name: Covered call sold at next expiration after every assignment
archetype_specific_benchmarks.description: No recovery-wait conditioning at all. Counterfactual for H-C-02 -- and a direct test of the charter's explicit non-negotiable rule against this exact behavior.

archetype_specific_benchmarks.name: Mechanical close-before-assignment
archetype_specific_benchmarks.description: Always closes the CSP for a loss rather than allowing assignment, regardless of ownership quality. Counterfactual for H-A-01.

archetype_specific_benchmarks.name: Unconditional hold-to-original-basis recovery
archetype_specific_benchmarks.description: No recovery horizon or thesis-invalidation exit; holds until the stock returns to original cost basis or forever. Counterfactual for H-A-04 (the parameterized recovery-bound sweep) -- H-A-02 itself, now the settled 'a bound must exist' constraint, is verified by implementation inspection rather than a backtest comparison.

archetype_specific_benchmarks.name: Unconditional assignment acceptance
archetype_specific_benchmarks.description: Accepts every assignment regardless of ownership_acceptability or p_severe_drawdown -- the opposite failure mode from BA-1. A CONTROL contrasting with H-A-01's conditional acceptance (accept only when ownership-acceptable); never a recommended policy on its own.

control_matrix.note: These are controls a real strategy must beat, not recommended strategies -- several are deliberately bad policies (BQ-2's single delta, BA-1/BA-3's two opposite mechanical extremes, BC-2's immediate-CC) included specifically so the eventual THETA policy has to prove it beats them, not because any of them should ever run live.

notes: B5 (random-entry matched) is the standard random-null reference for any archetype's entry-selection hypothesis (H-Q-01, H-H-01) -- it is not redefined per archetype, only re-run against each archetype's specific universe/DTE/structure so the matching stays honest per TRD's own B5 description.

No numeric result is recorded in this file. These are pre-registered comparison definitions (per the ablation protocol in docs/TEAM_CHARTER.md: BASELINE vs BASELINE+NEW_FEATURE, all else constant) -- populating results without a working backtester would be inventing performance numbers, which is explicitly prohibited.
